newsitem.title: UK: Standard Chartered dealing, FX profits up.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered dealing, FX profits up.

text.p: Dealing and exchange profits at Standard Chartered Plc rose to 134 million pounds in the six-months to June 1997 from 108 million in 1996, figures released on Wednesday showed.
StanChart, the London-based bank with a big Asia-Pacific region franchise, said its income from foreign exchange dealings was up to 108 million pounds from 80 million in the first-half of 1996.
The bank reported big profits from foreign exchange trading in the Far East where currency turmoil has been rife in recent months.
Chief Executive Malcolm Williamson told Reuters the bank had not experienced such a big effect on its profits from a translation into sterling before.

"The problem we have...is that we are very much a dollar-related bank, we either get our money in U.S. dollars or currencies that are linked to it or currencies that have depreciated even more against sterling over the last year," Williamson said.
He dismissed as "absolutely untrue" recent rumours in the foreign exchange markets that the bank had lost money in the volatility.
"We've had a very good record on this in the last few months," he said. "You get daily ups and downs, but we've managed our book tightly and well and it's continued through July," he said.
StanChart on Wednesday reported first-half, pre-tax profits of 435 million pounds against 448 million in the same 1996 period.
